questions.explanation: A precipitation reaction occurs when two soluble salt solutions are mixed together and an insoluble salt (precipitate) forms as a solid.

questions.stem: How is the insoluble salt separated from the mixture after a precipitation reaction?
questions.explanation: The insoluble precipitate is separated by filtration. The precipitate is then washed with distilled water to remove any soluble impurities, and dried.

questions.stem: To make barium sulfate (an insoluble salt), which two solutions could you mix?
questions.explanation: Mixing barium chloride solution with sodium sulfate solution produces insoluble barium sulfate as a precipitate, plus soluble sodium chloride in solution.

questions.stem: Why is the precipitate washed with distilled water during the preparation?

options.text: To remove soluble impurities from the surface of the precipitate
To change the colour of the precipitate

questions.explanation: Washing with distilled water removes any soluble salt residue that may be on the surface of the insoluble precipitate, ensuring a pure product.

questions.stem: According to solubility rules, which of the following salts is insoluble in water?
questions.explanation: Lead iodide is insoluble in water. Most chlorides are soluble, but lead chloride is an exception. Similarly, most iodides are soluble, but lead iodide is insoluble.

questions.stem: What would you observe when lead nitrate solution is mixed with potassium iodide solution?
questions.explanation: When lead nitrate and potassium iodide solutions are mixed, a bright yellow precipitate of lead iodide forms immediately.

questions.stem: Why can insoluble salts NOT be made by reacting an acid with a base?

options.text: Because acids do not react with bases
Because the salt formed would dissolve in the water produced, and you need the salt to be insoluble to separate it
Because insoluble salts do not exist
Because you need two soluble reactants that combine to form the insoluble product via precipitation

questions.explanation: Insoluble salts are made by precipitation: mixing two soluble salt solutions so that the ions combine to form an insoluble product. Acid-base reactions produce salts in solution, which cannot be easily separated if they are soluble.
